title: Coraline, CATAN and Sony Walkman join LEGO Ideas second 2026 review
summary: Three new fan designs have reached the 10K supporter milestone and entered the second LEGO Ideas review of 2026, though it's not yet known if any will become official sets.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Three fresh fan-made creations have qualified for the second LEGO Ideas review of 2026 after reaching the required 10,000 supporters on the official LEGO Ideas platform. The new entries are Coraline – The Pink Palace, based on the 2009 stop-motion film and featuring a detailed house interior, a brick-built Mantis Tractor and seven minifigures; CATAN – The Game & 3D Wall Art, a playable board game recreation with hidden details that transforms into wall art once finished; and Sony Walkman TPS-L2, a 520-piece, 1:1 scale build of the classic 1980s cassette player with moving controls.

These join a growing list of designs already sitting in this review round, which is edging closer to the 100-project cap ahead of the submission deadline on 7 September. Reaching this stage doesn't guarantee a set - LEGO's review team still has to decide which, if any, projects move forward. Results are expected to be announced in early 2026 for this... sorry, early next year.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is the official route for fan concepts to become real sets, so seeing beloved properties like Coraline and popular titles like CATAN progress is exciting for collectors and builders who back these projects. It's also a reminder of how community support directly shapes future official releases - worth knowing if you're thinking about backing a project yourself.

title: LEGO Super Mario Minifigures vs Interactive Figures: What's Changing in 2027
summary: New minifigure-style Mario sets are coming in January 2027, phasing out the theme's original interactive electronic figures. Here's how the two approaches compare.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Eight new LEGO Super Mario sets have been revealed, due to launch on 1 January 2027, and they'll feature traditional minifigures of Mario, Luigi, Peach and other Nintendo characters instead of the electronic interactive figures the theme has used since launch.

LEGO Super Mario first arrived in 2020 as a collaboration between the LEGO Group and Nintendo. Its big gimmick was an electronic Mario figure with a digital chest screen and eyes that reacted to special stickers on 2x2 tiles, playing sounds and music as you built and ran through course pieces. Interactive Luigi and Peach figures followed, alongside expansion sets, Character Packs, Power-Up Packs, a 2024 refresh of the Starter Courses, and Mario Kart-themed builds in 2025.

The upcoming 2027 wave swaps that tech-driven approach for standard minifigures, effectively retiring the interactive figure format in favour of a more traditional building experience.

## Why it matters
This is a notable shift in direction for one of LEGO's longest-running licensed themes. Fans who found the interactive electronics limited or gimmicky may welcome the change, while others who enjoyed the sound and light features may see it as a step back. It also signals that the LEGO SMART Play System, used in newer themes, may be taking over as the go-to interactive format going forward.

## What to watch next
More details on the full 2027 Super Mario line-up are expected as the January release date approaches. It's worth watching whether the LEGO Group confirms this is a full transition away from interactive figures across the theme, or just for this particular wave of sets.

It launches on 1 October via LEGO Stores and LEGO.com/Star-Wars, priced at £649.99 in the UK (US $799.99 / CAN $1099.99). Anyone who buys within the first 10 days will also receive an exclusive gift-with-purchase: 40897 Darth Vader's Lightsaber, a 174-piece set and the first villain's lightsaber to join LEGO's ongoing lightsaber collection.

UCS Star Wars sets are among the most sought-after in the hobby, and claiming the "longest LEGO set ever" title is a big deal for collectors and display builders alike.
